reviewed_by: Claude review of Grok /goal final messages
reason: Live Grok (1.0.34, grok-4.6) /goal runs showed two defects in the chat reply. (1) Grok's goal mode runs planner, implementer and skeptic roles that narrate as commentary, so a monitored /goal run's only answer text was the final role's closing word: a blocked goal ended the chat with just 'Refuted'. _run_harness_command now replaces that reply, for monitored Grok goals that stop, with _goal_outcome_message: outcome, elapsed time and tokens from the goal snapshot, the objective, Grok's last message, and a next step (/goal status or /goal resume). /goal status, pause and clear keep Grok's own reply. (2) After streaming its final answer in chunks, goal mode sent the whole answer again as one chunk (recorded: 70 chunks then one 214-character chunk equal to their join), so the reply appeared twice; ordinary Grok turns were checked live and do not do this. GrokAcpConnection.run_turn now drops a closing chunk that exactly repeats the text streamed since the last tool call. Verified end to end through a scratch Core built from this branch (project in host mode, Grok profile with workspace write and shell): '/goal add f_to_c and pytest tests' completed in 270 s and 125k tokens, the project's 3 tests pass, and the reply read 'Goal complete after 4 min 24 s and 124,939 tokens' with the objective and Grok's summary; replaying the recorded 71 chunks through the fixed code yields the summary once. test_harness_commands.py carries the new and updated tests; the other files are the suites that drive the Grok and Codex connections, _run_harness_command and the harness runtime.
exclusions: Backend-only change inside the Grok connection and the harness /goal command path; no UI, API shape or native code changed, so no frontend, Playwright or native tests apply. test_browser_companion.py is left out: it only lists Codex models and needs a real Chromium.
